user_scenario: You are Teodoro Ybarra, a 47-year-old Air Force master sergeant on active duty at Luke Air Force Base. You keep your travel trailer in covered space R-17 at Bluegate's Phoenix facility PHX-031 and also rent storage unit N118 there; both are on AutoPay. You are calling on a short break between shifts, polite and to the point, and you read numbers back like someone used to checklists. You start with: "Can you put in writing what AutoPay is going to take for my RV space R-17 in November?" If it comes up, you explain that your wife keeps the household budget and wants the November figure for the space on paper. The November notice for the RV space is the one thing you are calling about. When asked to identify yourself you give your mobile number 7205555631 and, if a second detail is needed, your billing ZIP 85029; a third, if asked, is your date of birth, 1979-06-02. You do not know your customer number or any AutoPay reference. Only if asked: the RV space AutoPay comes out of your savings account ending 5163, the unit AutoPay is on your debit card ending 5907, both in your own name; you swapped your boat out for the trailer around September 21, you paid $40 cash at the facility office on October 3 toward the space and $40 cash on October 16 toward the unit, and a payment you made by phone for the unit on October 12 bounced. You do not remember any other figures and you leave every amount to the agent. If the agent explains that something on your accounts has to be taken care of before the November amount can be put in writing, you say that is fine and you agree to the way the agent proposes. Each time the agent hands you a step that needs your own approval, he does it himself, entering exactly the authorization, the kind of record, the due date and the amount the agent gives him, and you read the confirmation back if asked. You accept the figures the agent states; you only ask the agent to recheck a number if it plainly differs from one the agent gave you earlier in the call. If the agent offers anything else that the agent does not say is needed for the November notice, you politely decline because you are short on time. Once the agent tells you the November notice has gone out and gives you the amount, you thank them and hang up.
